messages:

Subject: Question: How fast do deletions remove EU data from backups?

Hi Ben / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. One of the compliance items our DPO has flagged relates to user-initiated deletion requests for EU customers. Two specific asks:

1) When a user triggers a full-account deletion in our production tenant, what is the timeline until that data is fully removed from all backup tiers (hot snapshots, replicated region snapshots, and offsite cold archives)? We need a worst-case and typical path.

2) Do you provide any evidence we can share with auditors that a deletion was propagated (e.g., snapshot metadata, tombstone logs, or an expunge confirmation)? If so, what does that artifact look like?

We also need to understand whether backup copies ever leave the EU region during retention and how decryption/key-destruction ties into expunge.

Can you share a short written response and any artifacts (matrix, runbook excerpts) we can attach to our vendor review?

Appreciate it —
Anna
Anna Garcia
Head of Compliance, GridPay
anna.garcia@gridpay.com
+44 20 7788 1234

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Garcia <anna.garcia@gridpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 16:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Question: How fast do deletions remove EU data from backups?

Thanks Anna — good questions. High level answers below; I attached a short DR/retention matrix and a one-page summary.

TL;DR:
- Tombstone/mark-for-deletion: within ~24 hours of a user deletion event we mark object(s) as deleted across active stores.
- Hot snapshot/prefix cache pruning: typically 24–72 hours depending on ongoing replication windows.
- Expunge from standard replicated snapshots (rolling GC): typical 30 days; worst-case 45 days if caught in mid-window.
- Offsite cold archives: 60–120 days depending on class (we provide an expunge request tracking mechanism and can run targeted recovery/expunge jobs; see attached).

Evidence we can provide:
- Snapshot metadata showing tombstone marker and last-seen timestamp (CSV row per snapshot).
- Audit entry (log ID) for the expunge job and a signed confirmation PDF.
- Key-destruction certificate if the data was encrypted with a customer-managed key and the key was scheduled/destroyed.

Notes/constraints:
- For EU-region tenants we keep backups in-region by default; cross-region copies only occur when you opt into cross-region DR or during rare automated failover.
- If GridPay is using a customer-managed key (CMK) with KMS/HSM, destruction of that key effectively renders offsite encrypted archives unrecoverable — we can provide a key-wrapping/destruction certificate from our KMS partner as support.

I'll loop Rishi and Naomi for the exact timeline language and the artifacts you can expect for an auditor. Attaching: redwood-dr-matrix.csv, backup-retention-summary.pdf.

Best,
Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-dr-matrix.csv; backup-retention-summary.pdf)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Anna Garcia <anna.garcia@gridpay.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 16:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Question: How fast do deletions remove EU data from backups?

Anna — adding a few technical clarifications from the infra/security side.

1) "Mark-for-delete" vs expunge: when an account is deleted we create a tombstone in the primary metadata store; that tombstone prevents reads and starts the GC lifecycle. Tombstones replicate immediately, but the background GC sweep runs on a windowed schedule (we publish tenant GC windows as part of the contract — typical cadence: daily sweep, monthly deep purge).

2) Snapshots & incremental chains: incremental snapshots keep references to previous blocks. An expunge requires either rewriting the incremental chain or performing a targeted rewrite of affected snapshots (expensive). For practical compliance, we offer two options:
  - Scheduled expunge: we run a targeted expunge job for the tenant which rewrites snapshots to remove references (recommended for high-sensitivity delete requests).
  - Key destruction: if GridPay uses a CMK, destroying the key is an irrevocable way to ensure archives are unreadable; we will provide a key-destruction certificate.

3) Evidence artifacts we can provide to auditors:
  - Snapshot metadata dump (CSV) with snapshot_id, region, created_at, tombstone_flag, last_referenced_at.
  - GC job audit log lines (timestamped) and job output summary.
  - KMS key-destruction certificate if applicable.

4) Timelines (typical config for EU-only tenants):
  - Tombstone written: <24 hours.
  - Daily GC sweep: within 48 hours for hot tiers.
  - Targeted expunge job duration: 6–72 hours depending on dataset size; scheduled with customer.
  - Offsite cold archive retention: depends on archive class; expunge-by-rewrite can be 30–90 days.

I attached the internal key-destruction playbook excerpt for reference (redacted). If GridPay wants a test run, we can schedule a canary expunge on a synthetic tenant to produce the auditor artifact set.

—Rishi
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: key-destruction-playbook.docx)

Subject: Re: Question: How fast do deletions remove EU data from backups?

Thanks Ben / Rishi — that helps a lot. A couple quick follow-ups:

- For the targeted expunge option, can you confirm who schedules the job and what the SLA for completion is (GridPay requests it on a business day — what are realistic completion windows)?
- For the key-destruction certificate flow: if we use CMK, will Redwood hold any copy of the plaintext key material or does destruction occur solely in our KMS? We need to be clear in our vendor questionnaire.
- Can you produce a single-page auditor artifact (signed PDF) showing the snapshot metadata + GC job ID + timestamp for the canary run? That's what our DPO prefers.

If you can outline the process in bullet points (request -> approval -> scheduling -> execution -> confirmation artifact), that would be ideal. We may also ask for a redline to the contract deleting language once we confirm process.

Anna

Subject: Re: Question: How fast do deletions remove EU data from backups?

Anna — thanks for the clarifying questions. Below is a concise runbook we can follow; I put realistic completion windows and the artifact types we will provide. If that looks good I'll open a HubSpot request and schedule a canary expunge on a synthetic tenant (no production data) to produce the auditor PDF.

Proposed runbook (request flow):
1) Request: GridPay files an expunge request via our security portal (or we accept a signed email + PO if you prefer).
   - Required fields: tenant_id, dataset scope (account vs object), requested completion date, contact person.
2) Review & Approval: Redwood Security (Rishi) validates scope and schedules the job. Typical review turnaround: same business day (within 8 hours).
3) Scheduling: Operations schedules targeted expunge job into the next maintenance window. SLA options:
   - Standard: completion within 7 business days.
   - Expedited: completion within 48–72 hours (requires approval and additional fee).
4) Execution: Expunge job performs snapshot rewrite or targeted block removal. Duration depends on size — we provide an ETA before start (range 1–72 hours).
5) Confirmation artifact delivered within 24 hours of job completion:
   - Auditor PDF (signed): snapshot metadata extract + GC job ID + timestamp + operator signature.
   - CSV export: snapshot_id, region, tombstone_flag, last_referenced_at.
   - Optional: KMS key-destruction certificate if key destruction was used.

Notes on keys and jurisdiction:
- If GridPay uses Redwood-managed keys, Redwood will not destroy keys on your behalf; only customer-managed keys provide the guaranteed crypto-based unrecoverability.
- Redwood keeps EU-region backups in-region unless cross-region DR was explicitly enabled for your tenant; we will include region metadata in the auditor PDF.

Next steps I propose:
- Approve the runbook above and confirm whether you want a canary on a synthetic tenant (recommended).
- Naomi / Legal will draft the deletion confirmation language for the contract (we can provide recommended wording).

I'll open a HubSpot ticket and link the artifacts once the canary is scheduled.

Best,
Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment: confirmation-delivery-template.pdf)
